messages.author: 85710a48a204a0a6
messages.subject: 3-way latent variable interactions
parts:
Dear colleagues, 
I have read Schoemann & Jorgensen's excellent recent article for testing and interpreting latent variable interactions. The article however only provides example syntax for two-way interactions.

I was wondering if any of you had an example syntax for a three-way interaction? 

I am attempting a test of a model with three different latent variables (with 4, 3 and 3 indicators each) and wanted to make sure I was writing the "#Fix covariances between interaction and predictors to 0" and the "#Residual covariances between terms from the same indicator #covariances between the same indicator are constrained to equality" parts of the model correctly. 

Thank you.
Regards
GAT

messages.subject: Re: 3-way latent variable interactions
parts:
Hi GAT,

Take a look at the help pages for the probe3WayRC and prob3WayMC functions. There should be examples with 3 way interactions there.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: 3-way latent variable interactions
parts:
Sorry: an additional clarification for those of you who are familiar with this kind of model. In the article, I read "residual covariances should be estimated between product indicators that share a first-order indicator". If I understood this correctly X1.Z1 will covary with X1.Z2 and X1.Z3 because they all share the first-order indicator. Equality constraints can be applied. The syntax will look something like this:

X1.Z1 ~~ a*X1.Z2 + a*X1.Z3
X1.Z2 ~~ a*X1.Z3

But, with a three-way interaction, will the covariance between X1.Z1 and X1.Z1.W1 (and all the other possible combination including X1) will also be modelled using the same constraints? 

X1.Z1 ~~ a*X1.Z1.W1

Thanks

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: 3-way latent variable interactions
parts:
Ah, that's a really good question. I've been meaning to work on a paper related to three-way interactions among latent variables. Here's what I'd say (note: this is my opinion I don't have a simulation study demonstrating this (yet)):

If you have the same number of indicators for all first order latent variabels (X, Z, & W) and the indicators are congeneric (have similar factor loadings) I'd use a matched-pairs approach. This will greatly simplify your model compared to the all pairs approach

If you're using the all pairs approach with residual centering you should allow covariances of all product indicators based on the same item for latent interaction variables at the same level. So you'd estimate a residual covariance between X1.Z1 and X1.Z2 and X1.W1. For these you could then constrain them to be equal (to reduce the number of parameters to estimate)if they have the same first order indicator. For the three way interaction you would allow residual covariances between product indicators based on the same variable, e.g. X1.Z1.W1. and X1.Z1.W2, you'd constrain parameters to equality if they had the same pairs of indicators, e.g. X1.Z1.W1 and X1.Z1.W2 would be equal to X1.Z1.W1 and X1.Z1.W3. Note you do not have to include residual covariances between product terms for the 2-way and 3-way interactions since the residual centering process means that the 2-way interaction variables are uncorrelated with the 3-way interaction variables.

Hope that helps

Alex
